title: How to Connect Stripe to Airtable (3 Ways)
description: No native integration exists between Stripe and Airtable; here's how to bridge them with Zapier/Make or Stripe webhooks.
bodyHtml:
Stripe has no built-in Airtable integration, so teams that want payment and customer data mirrored into an Airtable base (for reporting, ops workflows, or a lightweight CRM) have to bridge the two with an automation tool or a small amount of custom code.

MethodSetup effortBest for
Zapier / MakeLow-mediumMost teams; no-code, covers common events
Airtable's native Stripe extensionLowRead-only dashboards inside an Airtable base
Stripe webhook + Airtable API (custom)HighTwo-way sync, custom field mapping, high volume

Method 1: Zapier or Make

The most common route. Typical setup for logging new payments:

  • Trigger: "New Payment" or "New Charge" in Stripe
  • Action: "Create Record" in Airtable
  • Map Stripe fields (amount, customer email, description) to Airtable columns

Both tools support other Stripe triggers too (new customer, subscription canceled, invoice paid), so you can build several small automations rather than one that tries to cover every event.

Method 2: Airtable's Stripe extension

Airtable has a built-in Stripe extension (in the Extensions marketplace) that displays Stripe data as a read-only panel inside a base, useful for a quick dashboard view. It doesn't write Stripe data into Airtable records, so it's not a substitute for Method 1 if you want that data queryable and filterable as normal rows.

Method 3: Stripe webhook + Airtable API (for developers)

For two-way sync, deduplication, or high event volume that would burn through a no-code plan's task limits, listen for Stripe webhook events (e.g. charge.succeeded, customer.subscription.updated) on your own endpoint, then upsert matching Airtable records via its REST API using the Stripe object ID as the match key:

PATCH https://api.airtable.com/v0/{baseId}/{table}/{recordId}
Authorization: Bearer {apiKey}
Content-Type: application/json

{ "fields": { "Status": "paid", "Amount": 4200 } }

Which to pick

Zapier or Make covers most use cases without code. Reach for the custom webhook approach once volume, two-way sync, or event coverage (Stripe has dozens of event types) outgrows what a no-code plan handles affordably.
